problem_statement: codrops/ProductGridLayout is a runnable static HTML/CSS/JS 'Responsive Product Grid Layout' Blueprint (Modernizr + a small vanilla-JS shop controller) served directly from static files, rebranded here as the 'Verdant Grove' outdoor-apparel shop. It has a fixed centered container with a header and a responsive grid of six product cards (rotate control, favourite, a size picker XL/L/M/S, a colour picker, price, and an add-to-bag control). The shop's OWN browsing is completed here with a native 'Shop by collection' category filter: a chip row (All / Everyday tees / Statement prints / Cosy layers) mounted above the product grid that shows/hides the real product cards by their data-category, plus a live count readout (class 'collectionfilter__readout', id #collection-readout) reading 'Showing N of 6 · <Collection>' that stays in sync with the filtered grid. The filter row + readout are styled by a dedicated stylesheet css/collectionfilter.css and the filter + live-count behaviour is wired by js/collectionfilter.js. In the current build FOUR things are wrong and must be repaired together while keeping the same product cards, the size/colour/favourite/rotate/add-to-bag controls, and the shop look: (A) the filter chip row uses a fixed pixel width with flex-wrap:nowrap and fixed-width chips, so on a 390px phone the chips cannot wrap and push the document wider than the viewport (a horizontal scrollbar appears) while desktop and tablet look fine; (B) the native filter + live-count readout must remain present and legible on the product grid, not collapse away; (C) the product grid must keep the shop's clean pine-green / white card look and grid geometry, not collapse into a dark pile of overlapping cards; and (D) clicking a collection chip must filter the grid AND update the live readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <Collection>' for that collection, not leave it frozen on the previous count. The fixes must live in the filter/readout layout+palette (css/collectionfilter.css) and the filter live-count wiring (js/collectionfilter.js); do not touch the product markup, the images, the size/colour pickers, or the shop's visual language.
required_content: The shop keeps its six product cards (image + title + price + size/colour/favourite/rotate/add-to-bag controls) and gains a native 'Shop by collection' category filter (chip row All / Everyday tees / Statement prints / Cosy layers) with a live count readout (#collection-readout) reading 'Showing N of 6 · <Collection>'.
The page no longer overflows horizontally at 390px: the filter chip row and the product grid wrap or shrink so the document width equals the phone viewport width.
The native filter chip row and the live-count readout are present and legible on the product grid (the collection host state), not collapsed away or buried.
The 'Verdant Grove · 3 collections · 6 pieces' collection-focus summary label greets the shopper in BOTH the header AND with the filter (the same label in both regions), not in only one region.
The product grid keeps the shop's clean pine-green / white rounded soft-shadow cards and grid geometry (no dark/near-black collapse or overlapping card pile).

Clicking a collection chip filters the product grid to that collection AND updates the live readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <Collection>'; the terminal state after a 'Statement prints' click reads 'Showing 2 of 6 · Statement prints', not a stale 'Showing 6 of 6 · All collections'.
Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts of the filter row, readout and product grid are visually preserved with no new overflow.

The rotate/favourite/size/colour/add-to-bag controls, the header, and the shop's visual language remain functional and reachable; the local product image assets continue to drive the product surfaces.
No JavaScript console errors or failed network requests are introduced on any captured state.
design_constraints: Match the existing pine-green / white card surfaces, box shadows, rounded product cards, centered container spacing, and shop typography for the filter row and readout.
The filter + readout should read as the shop's own shop-by-collection affordance, not a full hero replacement, modal, dashboard widget, or separate app shell.
The product cards must keep a clean grid, keep product images visible, and avoid overlapping or piling on top of each other.
The filter chip row must become responsive (wrap onto multiple rows and/or use a flexible chip basis) rather than relying on a fixed pixel row width with non-wrapping fixed-width chips.
Do not mask the overflow by clipping the row with overflow-x:hidden or shrinking the row width while keeping chips/cards from wrapping; the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport.
The native filter and live readout must stay present and legible on the grid state; hiding or collapsing them to dodge the visual gate is not acceptable.
The live-count wiring must re-read the filtered grid on every chip click; a handler that filters the grid but leaves the readout frozen on the previous count is not acceptable.
Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile states must avoid horizontal overflow and card overlap.
Only css/collectionfilter.css and js/collectionfilter.js change between the broken and repaired build; the product markup, images, and other controls stay the same.
state_constraints: desktop_home captures index.html at 1440px: the native 'Shop by collection' filter, the live 'Showing 6 of 6 · All collections' readout, the six product cards, and the collection-focus summary label in BOTH the header and with the filter render on-brand with no horizontal overflow.

mobile_home / mobile_collection capture the same page at 390px, where the broken fixed-width nowrap filter row + collapsed grid push the document wider than the viewport; the repaired filter removes that overflow.
desktop_collection / mobile_collection scroll the product grid + native filter into the viewport so their on-brand palette and grid geometry are judged visually (this is the D3 host).

desktop_filter_prints / mobile_filter_prints click the native 'Statement prints' collection chip and confirm the grid filters to the two statement-print cards AND the live readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Statement prints'; the mobile filter state must also be free of horizontal overflow after the repair.

desktop_filter_prints is the interaction terminal state: after clicking 'Statement prints' the readout must read 'Showing 2 of 6 · Statement prints', changed from 'Showing 6 of 6 · All collections' on desktop_collection.

Source inspection confirms the site is a static HTML template served directly; the six product cards carry data-category, css/collectionfilter.css controls the filter row + readout + grid layout/palette, and js/collectionfilter.js filters the cards and keeps the #collection-readout count in sync.

change_completion: The mobile page no longer overflows horizontally: document width equals the 390px viewport within tolerance.
The shop gains a native 'Shop by collection' filter and a live 'Showing N of 6 · <Collection>' readout; clicking 'Statement prints' updates the readout to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Statement prints'.
The native filter chip row and the readout are present and legible on the product grid.
design_consistency: The filter row, readout and product grid keep the pine-green / white rounded soft-shadow cards and on-brand typography (no dark near-black collapse).
Desktop and tablet appearance of the filter, readout and product grid is preserved.
The page remains the same shop, not a redesigned layout.
regression: The rotate/favourite/size/colour/add-to-bag controls, the header, and navigation remain functional and reachable.
The local product image assets continue to drive the product surfaces.
No console errors or failed requests are introduced on any captured state.
responsive: 390px home, collection and filter states have no horizontal overflow, card collisions, or clipped cards.
The filter chip row and product grid wrap or shrink cleanly on mobile while staying tidy on desktop/tablet.

author_notes: Repo-grounded static codrops ProductGridLayout shop (rebranded Verdant Grove). L4 harden of the shop's OWN native shop-by-collection browsing: a 'Shop by collection' category filter over the real six product cards (each tagged data-category), completed with a live 'Showing N of 6 · <Collection>' count readout. Content and DOM are byte-identical across reference/baseline/bad; the only source that varies between legs is css/collectionfilter.css and js/collectionfilter.js. Four orthogonal discriminators: no_horizontal_overflow (tol 24) on the mobile collection/filter states (reference 0px, baseline overflow, bad masked-but-still-overflowing); dom_assertions for the native filter + readout presence + filtered count; visual_regression on the scrolled collection states (the bad negative-margin collapse piles the real product cards into an illegible near-black heap); and interaction_assertions on the post-click readout (bad filters the grid but leaves the readout stale). Local product imagery keeps all three legs runtime-clean (0 console, 0 network, 0 overflow on the reference) across the seven captured states.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: codrops ProductGridLayout is a runnable static product-grid shop; used here to complete the shop's own browsing with a native shop-by-collection category filter over the real product cards plus a live count readout, whose responsive layout, visual fidelity, filter presence and interaction terminal state are the deterministic product-grade discriminators.
metadata.defect: native filter chip row uses a fixed-width nowrap row that causes mobile horizontal overflow; the product grid collapses into an overlapping near-black pile; and the live-count readout stays frozen on the previous count after a chip click
metadata.discriminator: no_horizontal_overflow (tol 24, mobile) + native-filter/readout dom_assertions + visual_regression on the collection states + category-filter interaction_assertions
